name: NLPCC2018
evaluation_notes: Original shared-task evaluation uses word-segmented MaxMatch/M2-style F0.5. Later papers may also report character-level F0.5, so unit must stay visible.
notes: Early large-scale CGEC benchmark built from Lang-8 learner data.
source: CGEC survey Sections 2.2 and Table 2, pages 10-11 and 23

name: MuCGEC
evaluation_notes: Original MuCGEC benchmark uses a character-based metric that merges char edits into spans; this is treated as the ChERRANT-style word/span F0.5 column.
notes: Evaluation-oriented multi-reference dataset drawn from several learner-data sources.
source: CGEC survey Sections 2.3 and Table 2, pages 11-12 and 23

name: YACLC
evaluation_notes: The source paper is a corpus/annotation release and does not report a test F0.5 leaderboard; add rows only when a published paper reports comparable YACLC scores.

name: FlaCGEC
domain: HSK reading corpus and proficiency-standards grammar examples
error_label_explicitness: explicit grammar points and edit types
evaluation_notes: Original FlaCGEC experiments report detection and correction F0.5 with MaxMatch/M2; the compact table uses correction F0.5 rows and marks the non-ChERRANT scorer.
notes: Useful for grammar-point coverage, but not directly comparable to naturally occurring corpora.

name: FCGEC
domain: public-school Chinese exams; supplemental error-free news sentences
evaluation_notes: Original FCGEC correction task uses MuCGEC character-level edit metrics: char edits are merged into spans and evaluated with F0.5.
notes: Native-speaker correction dataset with explicit operations and categories.
source: CGEC survey Sections 2.6 and Table 2, pages 15-16 and 23

name: MCSCSet
multi_reference: unknown / not reported in CGEC survey table
evaluation_notes: MCSCSet is a related medical-domain Chinese spelling correction dataset rather than a core CGEC rewriting benchmark. It is included here because Tan, Yang, and Xu (2023) report ChERRANT F0.5 alongside MuCGEC and FCGEC.
notes: Related CSC benchmark; compare within MCSCSet only.
source: Tan, Yang, and Xu (2023), CGEC survey Table 6, page 34; MCSCSet dataset paper

name: CCTC
domain: news, blogs, and popular science articles
evaluation_notes: The CCTC source paper reports F2 for native-speaker correction, not compact test F0.5; current F0.5 rows come from later NaSGEC transfer experiments.
notes: Complements sentence-level benchmarks with document-level native writing.
source: CGEC survey Sections 2.7 and Table 2, pages 16-17 and 23

name: NaCGEC
evaluation_notes: The NaCGEC source paper evaluates with word-level MaxMatch/M2 F0.5, while later L1 papers often use span-level ChERRANT-style F0.5.
source: CGEC survey Section 2.8 and Table 2, pages 17-18 and 23

name: NaSGEC
domain: social media, undergraduate theses, and exams
error_label_explicitness: no primary span labels; edit types post-extracted
evaluation_notes: The NaSGEC paper evaluates with a character-based metric: outputs and references are aligned to extract edits, then merged into spans for F0.5.
source: CGEC survey Section 2.9 and Table 2, pages 18-19 and 23

name: CEFE
error_label_explicitness: explicit in identification tracks; implicit in rewriting
evaluation_notes: Track 3 rewriting reports Test B F0.5 with MuCGEC-style edit metrics; Track 1 and Track 2 use F1-based official scores and stay separate.
notes: Essay fluency evaluation task with correction and identification views.
source: CGEC survey Section 2.10 and Table 2, pages 19-23
